title: dynamic-shard-attn-microkernel-and-rotary-offset-stitching-for-continuous-batching
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce a dynamic-shard microkernel that late-binds kernel selection to observed sequence-length/shard distribution and a rotary-offset stitching layer that aligns KV slices across continuous-batching boundaries; ~12% p99 latency reduction on long-context workloads and ~9% token-cost saving in continuous-batching scenarios.
description: Context: Production serving has increasing variance from mixed sequence-length workloads and multi-tenant continuous batching which creates suboptimal KV alignment and kernel selection. Motivation: reduce p99 latency and per-token cost without requiring model changes or new maintenance burden for ops. This PR introduces two orthogonal features: (1) a dynamic-shard attention microkernel (late-bound kernel selector and small-footprint microkernel implementations for skinny/short/long shards) and (2) rotary-offset stitching which fixes misaligned rotary/rope offsets when KV cache slices are split across continuous-batching boundaries. Summary of changes: added a late-bound kernel selector that picks optimized microkernels (small-tile, wide-tile, and wavefront microkernels) based on runtime shard shape; implemented a lightweight runtime registry for microkernels and a fast path for fused qkv->softmax->apply rotary for the small-tile microkernel; added a rotary-offset stitcher during KV assemble that recomputes per-shard rotary offsets and applies an O(1) remap for slices that straddle batch boundaries to avoid artifacts; updated continuous-batcher to emit shard-aligned KV slice metadata and a hint to the scheduler for prefetch alignment; improved the allocator to reserve KV padding when needed to maintain cache-line friendly alignment. API/compatibility: no API changes to the public inference REST/SDK surface; changes are internal to runtime and opt-in behind the flag runtime.dynamic_shard_attn=true. Performance: internal perf runs on c5g-like infra and NVidia A100 cluster show p99 latency improvements of 8-14% depending on mix, average token throughput improvements of 6-11% for mixed short/long workloads, and up to 9% token-cost reduction when continuous-batching is enabled because fewer fallback kernels are invoked. Safety/fallback: when runtime.dynamic_shard_attn is disabled or a microkernel fails feature checks, runtime falls back to current flashbridge kernel to guarantee correctness. Testing: unit tests for microkernels and rotary stitching added; integration perf harness with synthetic variable-length streams; CI includes determinism checks comparing output with baseline within L2 numerical tolerances. Rollout plan: staged rollout with canary on Dedicated for 24 hours, monitor p99 and correctness traces, then 25% traffic ramp to all dedicated clusters, fail-open to baseline kernel on anomaly. Related work/items: builds on earlier kernel registry work (ENG-8220) and continuous-batching scheduler heuristics (ENG-9120). Checklist: ensure changelog entry (done), add observability hooks for selected kernel (done), perf dashboard updated (done), security review completed (done).

review_conversation: Liam Chen: Can you explain the invariant that rotary-offset stitcher maintains across split slices? I worry about off-by-one artifacts when slices are not aligned to token boundaries.

Maya Patel: The stitcher computes a per-slice base_offset from original sequence absolute position and applies a modular remap using the model's rotary period; we added unit tests that compare against a monolithic KV write to ensure no drift. See tests/kv/test_rotary_stitcher.py for specifics.
Aisha Rahman: Microkernel selection looks good but the selector's cost model is simplistic. Can we include a learned or profile-driven threshold later?
Maya Patel: Agreed. This PR uses a heuristics-driven threshold tuned from our perf lab. Follow-up ENG-9680 will add profile-driven thresholds and online adaptation.
Diego Morales: Does this change alter memory accounting for RVs or KV caches? Need to ensure autoscaler alarms still work.

Maya Patel: We reserve worst-case padding in allocator and emit accounting events; I added a test for peak_memory reporting and updated autoscaler docs in docs/ops/rollout_notes/dynamic_shard_attn.md.
Liam Chen: Verified correctness on the canary cluster and re-ran perf bench; p99 improved and outputs match baseline within fp16 tolerances. Approving.
Aisha Rahman: Approved after confirming the fallback path covered by feature-flag gating.
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (p99 -12% on long-context sim, avg tokens/sec +9%)
perf_summary: Mixed-length job on A100: p50 +4% throughput, p95 +7%, p99 -12% latency on long sequences. Continuous-batching 8-client sim shows 9% lower token cost due to fewer kernel fallbacks and reduced KV misalignment stalls.
notes: Feature gated by runtime flag runtime.dynamic_shard_attn. Ops playbook updated and perf dashboards added. Follow-up items: ENG-9680 (adaptive thresholds), ENG-9711 (spill tuning for pinned shards).
